title: Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds
main_claim: On normal, irreducible, globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfolds, every sequence of generalized log canonical flips terminates. Here the boundary is rational, the fixed nef b-divisor is represented by an analytically nef Q-Cartier divisor on a projective modification, and each flip is a projective small diagram with the stated opposite ample signs. No scaling rule and no pseudo-effectivity assumption is needed.

issues.location: Sec. 2 (Propositions 2.x low-places / extraction / relative-program / gdlt-modification, Theorem special-termination), build/sections/02-preliminaries.tex
issues.description: Every relative-MMP input comes from the companion paper KahlerAuxiliary: continuation (Prop 9.7), one finite gklt run over a fixed bimeromorphic base (Prop 9.9), exact extraction (Prop 9.11), special termination (Thm 11.3) and the crepant gdlt modification in dimension 4 (Prop 11.4). Three more inputs come from CanonicalKahler: common models, analytic negativity and terminal smoothness in codimension two (Lemmas 2.1-2.3). This audit took them on trust. The paper states that these inputs do not use the companion's own fourfold termination or absolute MMP results, so no circularity was found. Soundness still depends on those companion statements holding exactly as quoted.
issues.evidence: 'The two assertions are respectively [KahlerAuxiliary, Propositions 9.7 and 9.9]' ... 'This is [KahlerAuxiliary, Theorem 11.3]' ... 'Its fourfold termination theorem is not an input.'

issues.description: The paper says the exceptional set V_Y is a proper analytic subset of codimension at least two with finitely many surface components, but it does not list everything that set must contain. It must also hold the surfaces where two labels meet, where a label is singular, and where the nef defect J is nonzero; the text folds all of these into 'loci where a label fails to be smooth and alone or the nef datum fails to descend'. This is correct but compressed. Each of these loci is a proper analytic subset of Y, so its surface components are finite. Not a gap.
issues.evidence: 'The complement of the isomorphism open, and the loci where a label fails to be smooth and alone or the nef datum fails to descend, are contained in a proper analytic subset of Y of codimension at least two.'

coverage: I read the whole proof. Section 1 has the main theorem and setup. Section 2 states the auxiliary inputs and their scope. In Section 3 I checked the common models, the nef defect, the singularity comparison, small-diagram comparison (support of F, dimension inequality), program comparison, the nef/ample lemma and cycle-class loss (Borel-Moore localization). In Section 4 I checked the terminal junction construction, including why the connector has no divisorial steps, and surface finiteness. For the latter I verified by hand: the self-intersection bound u_j <= 2/eps from adjunction, the negative-definite row-bound test vector (expanded the quadratic form), the column rank of the grouped matrix AP, the Hadamard/Cramer denominator, and the exclusion of recurring surface centres. In Section 5 I followed the branch inequality: the normalization excision sequence, strictness, the support bound i+z<=2 in the decomposition-theorem argument, H^1 vanishing on C, purity via Hodge-filtration preservation, and the cone/IC stalk estimate giving b_T. In Section 6 I followed the curve places: finite monodromy via Quot spaces, the Stein core, Fujino's local small Q-factorialization, injectivity of the degree map, and distinctness of the global divisors. In Section 7 I checked the echo discrepancies, finiteness below discrepancy two, the local bound q_Y(V) >= -(r_V^var - 1) (ceiling inequality, m_h >= r_{V,h}, at most one label with b > 1/2), the junction lower bound via the branch theorem, the normalization rank change and the exact difficulty change. In Section 8 I checked the positive-surface detector (N-lattice for a^+, ceiling weights), the strong gklt termination, gdlt termination via special termination and floor deletion (ample signs re-checked), the nonempty lift, and the main proof. I did not check the cited companion papers themselves.
sibling_notes: The board had one sibling entry for family 056: 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds' (rank 51, no gap found). Its minor notes are about projectivity of a contraction in its own Prop 6.4 and about the Hacon-Xie finiteness theorem, and neither affects this paper. The two papers share the KahlerAuxiliary companion inputs, and both audits had to take those on trust.
